full_judgment:
Md. Ansar Ali J: These two Rules one being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1222 of 1994 and the other being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1223 of 1994 arise out of 2 separate applications under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of accused petitioner Md. Anwar Hossain and Abdul Mannan Fakir respectively in connection with GR Case No. 118 of 1994 which arose out of Bogra Sadar PS Case No. 55(2) 94 under section 409 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Thana Magistrate Bogra Sadar, Bogra. Both the Rules are heard together and disposed of by the following judgment 

 One Md. Abdul Hye Khan, 877 Area Manager, Grameen Bank, Area Office of Shibganj lodged an First Information Report with the Bogra Sadar Police Station on 26-2-94 alleging, inter alia, that on 13-2-1994 some important papers were stolen from the Grameen Bank office situated at Namuja under Bogra Sadar Police Station and in that connection an ejahar was lodged on 15-2-1994 and accordingly, Bogra PS Case No. 28(2) 94 was started under sections 461/380 of the Penal Code and in that connection the accused petitioners were arrested but subsequently suspicion arose that there might be some misappropriation of bank's money also by the accused petitioners, hence the account of the said Bank was audited to verify the same and it transpired from the audit report that the Bank assistants of the said Grameen Bank accused Anwar Hosain and Abdul Mannan Fakir have misappropriated a huge amount of money to the tune of Taka 14,91,000.00 by showing false distribution of the Bank's loan money to fake loanees. It has been specifically alleged in the First Information Report that accused Anwar Hossain has misappropriated a sum of Taka 10,81,000.00 and co-accused Abdul Mannan Fakir has misappropriated a sum of Taka 4,10,000. 00. Hence the case being Bogra Sadar Police Station Case No. 55 dated 20-2-94 under section 409 of the Penal Code. 

 3. On the prayer of the Officer-in-Charge Bogra Sadar Police Station the accused petitioners were shown arrested in the later case on 28-2-94 and thereafter Daroga Md. Aminul Islam was entrusted with the investigation of the case. Accordingly the investigation started. 

 4. The petitioners meanwhile moved their successive applications for bail before the learned Magistrate Bogra Sadar Ka-Anchal but their prayer was rejected each time. Being thus unsuccessful in obtaining bail from the court of the learned Magistrate the petitioners moved separate applications for bail before the learned Sessions Judge, Bogra in both the cases. The learned Sessions Judge after hearing the application of accused petitioner Anwar Hossain in Criminal Misc. Case No. 342 of 1994 in connection with the other case under sections 461/380 of the Penal Code was pleased to grant him bail vide order dated 9-7-94 but after hearing the application for bail in Miscellaneous Case No. 344 of 1994 arising of the present case he was pleased to reject the application for bail vide order dated 23-7-1994. 

 Thereafter the accused petitioner Anwar Hossain moved the instant application for bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in this court and obtained the present Rule being Criminal Rule No. 1222 of 1994. The other co-accused Abdul Mannan Fakir being unsuccessful in obtaining bail from the learned Magistrate moved separate application for bail along with co-accused Anwar Hossain before the learned Sessions Judge, Bogra being the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 344 of 1994 and the same was heard by the learned Sessions Judge, Bogra who was pleased to reject his prayer for bail vide order dated 23-7-1994. Thereafter co-accused petitioner Abdul Mannan Fakir moved separate application for bail before this court under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained a Rule being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1223 of 1994. 

 5. Mr. Abdul Momen Talukder, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner Md. Anwar Hossain, submits that the petitioner is a Field Assistant of the Grameen Bank Najuma Branch within Bogra District who has no connection with any financial transaction of the Bank and that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case out of a conspiracy in the office. The learned Advocate further submits that since the date of lodging the First Information Report on 20-2-1994, the investigation has been started but the same has not been completed as yet and the accused petitioner has been in jail-hajat for about a year. It is further submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner with reference to section 167(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, that in view of non-completion of the investigation within the amended statutory period of 120 days, the petitioner is entitled to get bail and this point was specifically urged before the learned Sessions Judge but he has rejected the prayer for bail of the petitioner without taking into consideration that point and making any observation on the same. The learned Advocate further submits that accused petitioner Anwar Hossain has been suffering from serious illness inside the jail and the learned Sessions Judge to verify the same called for a report from the Civil Surgeon and Medical Officer of the Bogra Sadar Hospital and the report shows that accused petitioner, in fact, suffers from non-specific chest pain i.e. chronic Bronchitis, and for his treatment some medical investigation is necessary which is not possible at the jail hospital and hence, at least on humanitarian ground for proper medical treatment, the accused petitioner should be enlarged on bail. 

 7. Mr. Farid Ahmed, the learned Assistant Attorney-General with Mr. JK Pal, the learned Advocate appeared for the State and opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioners contending, inter alia, that the accused are involved in a serious case of misappropriation of loan money of the Grameen Bank which has been rendering some commendable services to the poor people of this country and that the audit report shows that they have misappropriated a huge sum of money of the Bank and that the investigation of the case has now been taken up by the CID and in the process they have sent some papers to the hand-writing expert for verification of some relevant signatures and consequently some time is being taken for completion of the investigation of the case and at this stage if the accused are enlarged on bail there is chance of their abscission and tampering with the witnesses. 

 8. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the application for bail and the connected papers and also we have seen the order sheet of the Magistrate's Court where the case is now pending and we find that a number of dates have been fixed for submission of police report but till now the investigation has not been completed and the police report has not been submitted as yet and the next date has been fixed on 29-1-1995. It also transpires from the order-sheet of the Magistrate's Court, that the learned Magistrate concerned was absent in court on different dates on different grounds and no order has been passed at any time to direct the investigation officer to expedite the investigation of the case though 120 days already expired long ago. In the instant case which is under section 409 of the Penal Code against the employees of the statutory Bank namely, Grameen Bank, as per the amended provision. of section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1985, 180 days is the period fixed for completion of the investigation but it appears that even that period of 180 days has also expired in this case and the investigation has not been completed as yet. The purpose for the fixation of the period of investigation is meant for speedy trial of the case and to save the accused from unnecessary harassment in jail custody by prolonging investigation. But from the wording of the said provision of law, it appears that the same is not mandatory but directory. Therefore, on the expiry of the period for investigation the accused cannot claim his bail as a matter of right and it is ultimately the discretion of the court to be exercised judicially in the facts and circumstances of each case. So far accused petitioner Anwar Hossain is concerned, it appears from the medical certificate annexed to the petition that he is really sick and he requires immediate medical investigation of his disease and also treatment therefor but such investigation is not possible inside the jail hospital as opined by the Civil Surgeon and Medical Officer and, in that view of the matter, accused Anwar Hossain deserves special consideration. Proviso to section 497 of the CrPC also provides for bail on the ground of sickness even in the case of a non-bailable offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. Since accused petitioner Anwar Hossain has been in jail custody for about a year and he has been suffering from illness and requires treatment outside the jail, we are in favour of granting him bail for limited period. Hence, the Rule in Misc. Case No. 1222 of 1994 is made absolute. Let accused petitioner Anwar Hossain S/o. Jabed Ali of village Krishna Chandrapur. Police Station Gabtali, District Bogra be enlarged on bail for a period of 3 (three) months from the date of his release on bail to the satisfaction of the Deputy Commissioner, Bogra on executing a bail bond of Taka 50,000.00 (fifty thousand) with two sureties of like amount, one of whom must be a lawyer. 

 9. So far accused petitioner Abdul Mannan Fakir is concerned, we are not in favour of granting him bail at this stage in view of the gravity of the offence as alleged and hence his prayer for bail is rejected for the present and the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1223 of 1994 is discharged but before parting with this Rule we like to observe that the investigation in the case must not be further delayed and if the investigation of this case is not completed within a month from the date of receipt of this order, the accused petitioner Abdul Mannan Fakir may however renew his prayer for bail in the court below and in that case the court should favorably consider his prayer for bail with sufficient surety.
